title: Computer Science Degrees Are WORTHLESS, Now Workers Are FURIOUS — Here’s Why
summary: Reaction compilation on 'CS degrees are worthless': entry-level collapse stats, AI replacing juniors, mixed pushback.

assertions.quote: Entry-level hiring across all tech saw a 73% decrease ... structural elimination of the entry-level role

verdicts.note: Stanford 'Canaries' (2025) found ~13% relative employment decline for 22-25-year-olds in AI-exposed jobs, but rates, over-hiring correction and other macro factors also matter.

assertions.quote: One senior engineer today with AI can do the work of 10 engineers in the past world

verdicts.note: No measured study shows anything near 10x; field data put average gains around 10-20% and experts on mature code sometimes slow down.
Anthropic self-reports an average +50% productivity boost, with only 14% of respondents above +100%, far from 10x even among heavy early adopters at an AI lab.

assertions.quote: the computer science degree is done

verdicts.note: CS grad unemployment rose (~6-7%) but CS still has high median earnings and employment; the degree's value fell somewhat, not 'most' of it.

assertions.quote: They're saying AI, but ultimately, I don't think it's AI ... they over-hired in the pandemic

verdicts.note: The 2022-23 decline began before ChatGPT and tracks rate hikes and over-hiring; most economists attribute it mainly to macro factors, though AI may weigh on junior roles since 2024.
